clue.text: Preserve the flower to make tobacco

parts.note: to preserve food is to can it
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Someone dries and keeps a bloom to roll into a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaster is a coarse dried leaf sold for smoking in pipes.

clue.text: Unable to get an alternative singer

parts.note: unable means can't, written without the apostrophe
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A performer cannot find an understudy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor leads the chanting in a synagogue or church choir.

clue.text: A composition written on this, perhaps

definitions.text: A composition written on this, perhaps

parts.words: A composition written on this, perhaps
parts.note: a school essay or a piece of music, written down, would go on sheets for writing letters; the musical sense of the first half is the hint

explanation.surface: A suggestion of where a piece of work might be written.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing sheets for letters are what a composition, or a musical note, would be set down on.

clue.text: Money earned for reversing mines closure

indicators.note: reversing tells us the word for mines is read from right to left

parts.note: mines are pits
a closure is an end

explanation.surface: Pay handed out because coal mines are being reopened.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed salary, especially a cleric's.

clue.text: Characteristic beliefs held by the prophet Hosea

indicators.note: held by means the letters are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: The core convictions of the Old Testament prophet Hosea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the distinctive spirit and attitudes of a group or culture.

clue.text: Lengthy denunciation of one in business

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the word for business

parts.note: trade is commerce, business
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in commerce delivers a long angry rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism.

clue.text: Base for rising soldier of lofty character

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
noble means high-minded, of lofty character

explanation.surface: A soldier promoted from the ranks proves high-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns GI into IG. 'Base' looks like a military base but is the adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble and base both mean dishonourable or mean-spirited.

clue.text: One in a clerical robe I excuse

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the robe

parts.note: an alb is a white vestment worn by clergy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A priest offers a pretext while in his vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as a plea or pretext.

clue.text: Is 'e nagging, maybe? No. quite charming

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Is he a nag? Not at all, he is rather delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e is the dropped-aitch 'he'; its E joins NAGGING as anagram fodder, signalled by 'maybe'. The scan prints 'No.'; read it as 'No,'.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means attractive and pleasing, winning one over.

clue.text: Appeals in a race with improvised carts

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

indicators.note: improvised suggests the letters are put together in a new makeshift order

explanation.surface: Homemade go-karts draw a crowd at a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that attracts draws people to it, which is to appeal.

clue.text: All the same, it couldn't' be how the char got housemaid's knee

definitions.meaning: all the same means nevertheless, in spite of that

definitions.text: it couldn't' be how the char got housemaid's knee
definitions.meaning: a cleaning lady's knee complaint comes from kneeling to scrub, so it was not got by being upright

explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning woman; housemaid's knee is inflammation from kneeling. The printed apostrophe after couldn't is a stray mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding means nevertheless; split up it reads 'not with standing'.

clue.text: Ironwork knocked back-to-front in crush

indicators.note: knocked back-to-front means the last part of the word is moved to the beginning

parts.note: iron gives PRESS (to iron clothes) and work gives OP (opus)

explanation.surface: Wrought ironwork is buckled and smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron is PRESS and work is OP; moving OP to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to crush or keep down by force.

clue.text: Holding up bishop during his investiture

indicators.note: during places the chess abbreviation within the ceremony

parts.note: robing is the putting on of ceremonial dress at an investiture
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is delayed while being installed.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding up a bank or person means committing robbery.

clue.text: The same inside story is now widespread

indicators.note: inside puts the Latin word within the tale

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic story
idem is Latin for the same, used in references

explanation.surface: Gossip now goes round the same as before.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic disease is prevalent and spreading through a population.

clue.text: Infatuated girl with a strange song

parts.note: mad about someone means infatuated

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of girl and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovesick girl sings an odd tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Two Poles talking in the City

indicators.note: talking means the letters are spoken as their names

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: Two Polish visitors chat in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' means S and N are said aloud, 'ess-en'. 'Poles' looks like people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr.

clue.text: They may adjust and determine wages

parts.note: to set is to fix or determine
screw is old British slang for wages

explanation.surface: Bosses that tweak and fix pay rates.
explanation.definitionFit: Small screws used to fix or adjust parts in machinery.

clue.text: A good sort, the cricketer, but gets criticism

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, generous person
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A decent cricketer is nonetheless criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a hostile remark, originally a piece of brick thrown.

clue.text: The King of Arms, they say, is thinner

annotationWithheld.why: The King of Arms, they say, is thinner (5): RARER = thinner, but no King of Arms title found that sounds like the answer; parse unknown.
annotationWithheld.clue: The King of Arms, they say, is thinner

clue.text: Determination of heartless old official to invest foreign currency

indicators.note: to invest means to surround, so the money goes inside
heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval local official
the sol was the currency of Peru

explanation.surface: A gutted old bureaucrat tries to put money abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle letter of the official, and 'to invest' has that shortened word surround the currency; invest here means besiege, not put money into.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firmness of purpose, determination.

clue.text: Aversion to girl's predilection

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, here with the possessive S
a taste for something is a liking

explanation.surface: Hatred of a young woman's preferences.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion.

clue.text: Quite an unusual relic of old times

indicators.note: unusual means the letters appear in an unaccustomed order

explanation.surface: A rare object surviving from history.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an old object valued for its age.

clue.text: At one time cared about being ruined, it's said

indicators.note: it's said indicates the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: ruined means wrecked

explanation.surface: Someone once looked after something that has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: To reck is an archaic verb meaning to heed or care.
explanation.definitionFit: Recked is the old past tense of reck, to take heed or mind.

clue.text: Deficit in information agency amounts to very large figures

indicators.note: in places the shortfall inside the agency initials

parts.note: COI was Britain's Central Office of Information
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A government publicity body's shortfall reaches huge sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are huge statues, giant figures.

clue.text: The sign of an artistic politician

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A creative MP gives an indication.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is a sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: It may be the object

definitions.meaning: the word the is the definite part of speech of this kind
an object is a thing, an item

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' and 'a' are articles; an article is also any particular item.

clue.text: A theologian the French confused

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French divine is muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Addle as an adjective means muddled, as in addle-headed.

clue.text: Absurd bank squabble due to economy of course

indicators.note: absurd means the letters are put into a nonsensical new order

explanation.surface: A ridiculous row at the bank about cost-cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage: an economical course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrifty fry-up of leftovers served as part of a meal.

clue.text: Drawing equipment for making copies

definitions.meaning: harness straps by which a horse pulls a cart
copies a drawing through thin paper

explanation.definitionFit: Traces are harness straps for pulling; to trace is to copy an outline.

clue.text: Delivered cooked eels, dear?

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are doctored or rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner asks if the eels have been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns EELS DEAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means set free or delivered from captivity.
